purpose: Define the complete, compilable shape of monokl's workspace/extract config cluster -- TsconfigMode, WorkspaceOptions, and ExtractRequest -- per docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md Section 4 (lines 605-638), so a developer implementing workspace construction or the extract command never has to guess a variant, a method signature, a field, or which of these three types can even appear in JSON at all. TsconfigMode and WorkspaceOptions carry no serde derive whatsoever (#[derive(Debug, Clone)] only) -- the same zero-JSON-contract consequence LineHit established in SPEC-006 AC-015, here extended to a mixed unit-and-tuple-variant enum (TsconfigMode) and, for the first time in this project, to a struct with a genuine callable API surface (WorkspaceOptions::new, WorkspaceOptions::with_tsconfig) rather than a plain data-only struct. ExtractRequest, by contrast, does derive Serialize+Deserialize and is the actual type behind two docs/spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md Part 1 findings (#15 and #23) but never directly locked until now: finding #15, already cited elsewhere in this project's specs as precedent for a different type (SPEC-006 AC-004, for the structurally analogous CodeBlock), documents that a swapped line_start/line_end pair doesn't merely deserialize without error but has a specific, documented downstream behavioral consequence -- the extract command silently returns an empty result rather than erroring; finding #23, not previously cited by any prior spec in this project, documents that line_start: 0 is accepted despite the codebase's 1-indexed convention elsewhere. This track locks ExtractRequest's own shape and states both findings' precise, already-documented consequences for this exact type.
scope: TsconfigMode (a 3-variant enum mixing two unit variants and one 1-tuple variant, no serde derive, no Copy since its tuple variant wraps a non-Copy Utf8PathBuf, no PartialEq/Eq, no Default), WorkspaceOptions (a 2-field struct, no serde derive, with a 2-method impl block: a new constructor taking impl Into<Utf8PathBuf> and a #[must_use]-marked with_tsconfig builder step), and ExtractRequest (a 3-field struct, Serialize+Deserialize, camelCase) -- all verbatim per 01-core-architecture.md:605-638. It locks: each type's exact field/variant order and derive list; TsconfigMode's and WorkspaceOptions' total absence of a serde contract as a compile-time-only consequence; WorkspaceOptions::new's and with_tsconfig's exact signatures, including the impl Into<Utf8PathBuf> parameter type and the asymmetric presence of #[must_use] on only one of the two methods; that TsconfigMode has no Default impl of its own, so WorkspaceOptions::new's choice of TsconfigMode::Auto is a WorkspaceOptions-level decision, not one sourced from any trait on TsconfigMode; ExtractRequest's exact field shape and Option<usize> leniency for line_start/line_end; and ExtractRequest's precise, already-documented connection to docs/spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md Part 1 findings #15 (a swapped line range silently returns an empty result, not an error) and #23 (line_start: 0 is accepted despite the codebase's 1-indexed convention).
non_goals: All other Section 4 types not in this cluster -- SymbolKind/Visibility/SymbolEntry (SPEC-003), the dependency/export/JSX/LangData cluster (SPEC-005), the result/diagnostic primitives (SPEC-006), and the search-command request/response types (SPEC-007).

The extract command's own implementation of how it handles a swapped line_start/line_end pair to produce an empty result (finding #15), or how it decides to accept line_start: 0 (finding #23) -- this track locks ExtractRequest's own type shape and states both findings' already-documented behavioral consequences precisely; it does not re-derive or re-verify the extract command's internal logic beyond what those findings already state.

Whether ExtractRequest's line_start/line_end should gain validation (e.g. rejecting a swapped range or a zero value) -- this spec documents the current, verbatim, unenforced behavior; deciding whether to add validation is a behavioral decision for whichever track implements the extract command.

WorkspaceOptions' or TsconfigMode's actual runtime usage inside workspace-construction code (e.g. how TsconfigMode::Manual's wrapped path is resolved, or how TsconfigMode::Auto's auto-detection behaves) -- this track locks only the two types' own field/variant/method shapes as declared, not the workspace-construction logic that consumes them.

Whether TsconfigMode or WorkspaceOptions should gain a serde derive in the future -- this spec documents their current, verbatim absence of one and its compile-time consequence; it does not evaluate whether adding one would be desirable.

api_surface.name: WorkspaceOptions::new
api_surface.signature: pub fn new(root: impl Into<Utf8PathBuf>) -> Self
api_surface.description: 01-core-architecture.md:619-624. Constructs a WorkspaceOptions with root set from root.into() and tsconfig set unconditionally to TsconfigMode::Auto. The root parameter is an anonymous generic constrained by Into<Utf8PathBuf>, not a bare Utf8PathBuf, so callers may pass &str, String, or Utf8PathBuf. Carries no #[must_use]. See AC-004.

api_surface.name: WorkspaceOptions::with_tsconfig
api_surface.signature: #[must_use] pub fn with_tsconfig(mut self, mode: TsconfigMode) -> Self
api_surface.description: 01-core-architecture.md:625-629. Consumes the receiver by value (mut self), sets tsconfig to the given mode, leaves root untouched, and returns Self for fluent chaining. #[must_use] makes discarding the return value a compile-time warning, not an error. See AC-005.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: TsconfigMode (01-core-architecture.md:605-610) compiles with #[derive(Debug, Clone)] only -- no Serialize, no Deserialize, no Copy, no PartialEq, no Eq, no Default, no non_exhaustive -- and exactly 3 variants in this order: Auto (a unit variant, no associated data), Manual (a 1-tuple variant wrapping a single Utf8PathBuf field), Skip (a unit variant, no associated data). This is a mixed enum -- Manual carries data while Auto and Skip do not. Copy is absent not by arbitrary choice but because it could not be derived even if requested: Utf8PathBuf does not implement Copy, and a type containing a non-Copy field in any variant cannot itself derive Copy.

TsconfigMode has no serde derive of any kind and therefore no JSON representation whatsoever -- the same zero-contract consequence LineHit establishes in SPEC-006 AC-015, here extended to a type with a data-carrying tuple variant rather than a plain struct. TsconfigMode cannot be serialized or deserialized directly, and cannot be a field of any struct that itself derives Serialize or Deserialize without a manual custom implementation; attempting either produces a compile-time failure, not a runtime failure or a silently-wrong JSON shape -- rustc rejects the derive with an unsatisfied-trait-bound diagnostic (E0277) naming TsconfigMode specifically as the type missing the required impl, the same class of error SPEC-006 AC-015 establishes for LineHit. Because Manual's wrapped Utf8PathBuf field has no bearing on this outcome (the absence of Serialize/Deserialize applies at the enum level, to all three variants uniformly, regardless of which variant carries data), TsconfigMode's mixed unit/tuple shape does not change this conclusion from what a plain unit-only enum would produce.

WorkspaceOptions (01-core-architecture.md:612-616) compiles with #[derive(Debug, Clone)] only -- no Serialize, no Deserialize -- and exactly 2 fields in this order: root: Utf8PathBuf, tsconfig: TsconfigMode. Like TsconfigMode (AC-002), WorkspaceOptions has no JSON representation whatsoever and cannot be serialized or deserialized directly; attempting to use it where a Serialize/Deserialize bound is required is a compile-time E0277 failure naming WorkspaceOptions specifically, not a runtime one. This is doubly true given tsconfig's own type (TsconfigMode) also lacks Serialize/Deserialize -- even had WorkspaceOptions itself attempted to derive Serialize/Deserialize, it would fail to compile on the tsconfig field alone.

WorkspaceOptions::new (01-core-architecture.md:619-624) has the exact signature pub fn new(root: impl Into<Utf8PathBuf>) -> Self -- the root parameter is declared as impl Into<Utf8PathBuf>, an anonymous generic constrained by the Into trait, not a bare Utf8PathBuf. This is a real signature detail, not an equivalent simplification: a caller may pass any type implementing Into<Utf8PathBuf> (for example a &str or String, both of which camino's Utf8PathBuf provides conversions from, in addition to an already-constructed Utf8PathBuf), and the function body converts via root.into(). new sets tsconfig to TsconfigMode::Auto unconditionally -- the caller cannot influence tsconfig's initial value through new itself; doing so requires the separate with_tsconfig builder step (AC-005). new carries no #[must_use] attribute.

WorkspaceOptions::with_tsconfig (01-core-architecture.md:625-629) has the exact signature pub fn with_tsconfig(mut self, mode: TsconfigMode) -> Self, carrying a #[must_use] attribute directly above the method. The method takes self by value (mut self, not &mut self or &self), mutates its own local binding's tsconfig field to the given mode, leaves root untouched, and returns the same Self by value -- the classic Rust builder/fluent-chaining pattern, consuming the receiver rather than mutating in place. #[must_use] causes rustc to emit a compile-time WARNING, not a hard error, when a caller discards the returned Self without binding or chaining it further (for example, calling opts.with_tsconfig(mode); as a bare statement) -- code that does this still compiles and runs, just with a lint warning. This is an asymmetry worth stating precisely rather than assuming uniformly: new (AC-004) carries no #[must_use] of its own, only with_tsconfig does.

TsconfigMode has no #[derive(Default)] and no hand-written impl Default anywhere in its declaration (01-core-architecture.md:605-610) -- unlike SearchOptions and SearchLimits (SPEC-007 AC-001/AC-004), which each carry a hand-written impl Default even though it turned out to be inert for serde deserialize, TsconfigMode has no Default of any kind to be inert or otherwise: there is no way to write TsconfigMode::default() anywhere in the codebase without a manual impl this spec does not lock. WorkspaceOptions::new's choice to initialize tsconfig as TsconfigMode::Auto (AC-004) is therefore a decision encoded directly in WorkspaceOptions::new's own function body, not a value sourced from any trait implementation on TsconfigMode itself -- TsconfigMode::Auto has no more claim to being TsconfigMode's "default" variant at the type level than Manual or Skip do; it is simply the specific variant new's author chose to write.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Distinguishing 'WorkspaceOptions::new happens to pick TsconfigMode::Auto' from 'TsconfigMode::Auto is TsconfigMode's Default value' is a precise, easily-blurred distinction given this project's established pattern (SPEC-007) of hand-written Default impls existing but being inert for a different reason (missing #[serde(default)]) -- here there is no Default impl at all, a categorically different absence worth not conflating with SPEC-007's finding.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: ExtractRequest (01-core-architecture.md:632-638) compiles with #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)] and #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")], with exactly 3 fields in this order: file: Utf8PathBuf, line_start: Option<usize>, line_end: Option<usize>. No field carries any field-level serde attribute.

file is required on deserialize: a JSON object omitting "file" fails with a missing-field error naming that field. line_start and line_end, both Option<usize> with no field-level attribute, each independently tolerate a missing or explicitly-null key and deserialize to None (the pattern established in SPEC-003 AC-005 and reapplied throughout this project's prior tracks) -- a JSON object supplying only "file" (omitting both "lineStart" and "lineEnd") deserializes successfully with both fields None; a JSON object with "lineStart": null and "lineEnd": null deserializes identically. ExtractRequest carries no #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] attribute: deserializing a JSON object that includes an extra key not among the 3 named above succeeds, silently discarding the unrecognized key, the same unknown-key-tolerant behavior SPEC-003 AC-006 and SPEC-006 AC-003/AC-010 establish for SymbolEntry, CodeBlock, and Diagnostic.

A present (non-null) "lineStart" or "lineEnd" value follows the same three-way numeric rule SPEC-007 AC-006 establishes for SearchLimits' usize fields, applied here to line_start/line_end: (1) an integer-lexical literal (no fractional or exponent part) within 0 to 18446744073709551615 (u64::MAX) succeeds, deserializing to the corresponding Some(N); (2) an integer-lexical literal that is negative but within i64 range (down to -9223372036854775808, i64::MIN) fails with an invalid-value error, e.g. "invalid value: integer `-1`, expected usize"; (3) any literal written with a fractional or exponent part (e.g. 1.5, 5.0, 5e0) -- regardless of whether its value is a whole number -- OR an integer-lexical literal one past either boundary (18446744073709551616 or -9223372036854775809, reinterpreted as floating point) fails with an invalid-type error instead, e.g. "invalid type: floating point `1.5`, expected usize"; (4) a literal whose magnitude exceeds finite f64 range entirely (e.g. 1e309) fails at parse time with "number out of range", before any type dispatch, naming neither usize nor any other type. This is three rejection classes, not two -- SPEC-007 AC-006 states this explicitly ("three rejection classes in total ... not two") for the structurally identical SearchLimits fields, and this criterion mirrors that established rule rather than a narrower two-class characterization an earlier draft incorrectly attributed to it. SPEC-003 AC-012 is not cited as establishing this same three-class distinction: it names the invalid-value class for a negative SymbolEntry.line but states only that a non-integral value "likewise fails to deserialize" without naming that second case's error class, so it does not itself establish a class distinction the way SPEC-007 AC-006 does.

No source document states or enforces that ExtractRequest's line_start, when both fields are present, is less than or equal to line_end -- ExtractRequest derives Deserialize with no custom validation and no cross-field constraint carries this invariant, so a JSON object with lineStart: 100, lineEnd: 5 deserializes successfully as-is, structurally identical to the unenforced invariant SPEC-006 AC-004 establishes for CodeBlock's line_start/line_end. CodeBlock's own analogous gap is likewise documented with a consequence, a different one: 01-core-architecture.md:1217-1219's overlaps_significantly comment (quoted in SPEC-006 AC-004) states the unenforced invariant makes an underflow panic "a real possibility, not a theoretical one," defended against internally via saturating_sub. ExtractRequest's documented consequence is a distinct one: docs/spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md Part 1 finding #15 states it precisely: "extract never validates line_start <= line_end; a swapped range silently returns an empty (not erroring) result." This track locks ExtractRequest's own unenforced type-level shape and states finding #15's already-documented consequence precisely; it does not re-derive or re-verify the extract command's own internal logic that produces the empty result, per non_goals.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Citing finding #15's specific, already-documented behavioral consequence (silent empty result) rather than merely restating the unenforced-invariant pattern already established for CodeBlock required care to attribute the consequence correctly to the extract command's own logic (out of this track's scope) while still stating it as directly relevant, verified context for the type this track locks.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: No source document states or enforces a lower bound on ExtractRequest.line_start or line_end -- both are Option<usize>, and usize's own valid range includes 0, so a JSON object with lineStart: 0 deserializes successfully to Some(0), just as any other non-negative integer would. docs/spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md Part 1 finding #23 documents this precisely for this exact field: "extract --line-start 0 isn't rejected despite the codebase's 1-indexed convention elsewhere." This track locks ExtractRequest's own type-level shape, under which 0 is not distinguished from any other valid usize value; it does not re-derive independently why the rest of the codebase is 1-indexed or resolve whether line_start: 0 should be rejected, per non_goals -- finding #23 is cited as the source of the 1-indexed-convention claim, not re-verified from first principles here.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Finding #23's claim about "the codebase's own 1-indexed convention elsewhere" is taken as given from the cited finding rather than independently re-derived from every other line-number-bearing type in the corpus, since re-deriving that broader convention is outside what a type-shape lock on ExtractRequest itself can establish -- the citation is the grounding, not an independent re-confirmation of the wider convention.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A JSON object where "file" is present but holds a JSON type other than a string (a number, boolean, null, array, or object) fails to deserialize with an invalid-type error naming the found type and expecting a UTF-8 path string, not the generic "expected a string" text serde's own derived string-visitor would produce for a plain String field -- e.g. {"file": 5} fails with "invalid type: integer `5`, expected a UTF-8 path string", {"file": true} fails with "invalid type: boolean `true`, expected a UTF-8 path string", {"file": null} fails with "invalid type: null, expected a UTF-8 path string", {"file": []} fails with "invalid type: sequence, expected a UTF-8 path string", {"file": {}} fails with "invalid type: map, expected a UTF-8 path string", and {"file": 5.5} (a non-integral JSON number, also within the "number" case above) fails with "invalid type: floating point `5.5`, expected a UTF-8 path string" -- serde renders a JSON array as "sequence" and a JSON object as "map" in the found-type position, not as "array"/"object", so the error text's vocabulary for these two cases differs from the JSON type names this criterion's own enumeration uses. This wording comes from camino's own custom Deserialize implementation for Utf8PathBuf, not from a generic serde_json string-type mismatch: file: Utf8PathBuf is a camino-owned type with its own hardcoded expecting text, distinct from how a bare String field's type mismatch would read. Unlike line_start/line_end (Option<usize>), file: Utf8PathBuf carries no Option wrapper, so an explicit null value for "file" is a type-mismatch failure, not a tolerated missing-equivalent -- this extends AC-008's required-on-omission finding for file to the null and wrong-type cases specifically.

A JSON object where a present (non-null) "lineStart" or "lineEnd" holds a JSON type other than a number -- a string, boolean, array, or object -- fails to deserialize with an invalid-type error naming the found type: {"lineStart": "5"} fails with "invalid type: string \"5\", expected usize", {"lineStart": true} fails with "invalid type: boolean `true`, expected usize", {"lineStart": []} fails with "invalid type: sequence, expected usize", and {"lineStart": {}} fails with "invalid type: map, expected usize" -- as with AC-012's analogous cases for file, serde renders a JSON array as "sequence" and a JSON object as "map" in the found-type position, not as "array"/"object". The Option<usize> leniency AC-008 establishes extends only to a missing key or an explicit JSON null value; it does not extend to any other non-numeric JSON type supplied for a present value.

linked_research: docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md Section 4 (TsconfigMode, WorkspaceOptions, ExtractRequest verbatim declarations, lines 605-638 -- the primary source for all three types in this track); docs/spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md Part 1 finding #15 (ExtractRequest's swapped-range silent-empty-result behavior, AC-010, already cited as precedent by SPEC-006 AC-004 for the structurally analogous CodeBlock but locked directly here for the first time) and finding #23 (ExtractRequest's line_start: 0 non-rejection, AC-011 -- not cited by any prior spec in this project, unlike finding #15); .claude/specs/SPEC-003.json (AC-005, AC-006, AC-012 established Option-leniency, unknown-key-tolerance, and negative-usize-rejection findings, reapplied at AC-008/AC-009); .claude/specs/SPEC-006.json (AC-003, AC-004, AC-015 established unknown-key-tolerance, unenforced-invariant, and no-serde-derive-is-a-compile-time-fact findings, reapplied and in AC-010's case directly extended with a concrete documented consequence rather than left as a bare unenforced gap); .claude/specs/SPEC-007.json (AC-001/AC-004's hand-written impl Default precedent, distinguished rather than conflated with at AC-006, where no Default exists at all).
revision_note: First draft, produced under the same corner-case-first methodology established for SPEC-006/007: enumerated per-type corner cases before drafting, including for this cluster's two non-serde types (TsconfigMode, WorkspaceOptions) the specific consequence of their mixed variant kinds (TsconfigMode) and their genuine callable API surface (WorkspaceOptions) -- the first non-empty api_surface since SPEC-005. Deliberately distinguished this track's 'no Default impl exists at all' finding (AC-006) from SPEC-007's superficially similar 'a Default impl exists but is inert for serde' finding, rather than assuming the two clusters share the same underlying mechanism. ExtractRequest's AC-010/AC-011 deliberately cite docs/spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md findings #15/#23 as already-established, specific behavioral consequences for this exact type. Corrected after canon-verifier's grounding pass: only finding #15 was previously cited elsewhere in this project's specs, as precedent for a different, structurally analogous type (CodeBlock, SPEC-006 AC-004) -- finding #23 is cited for the first time by this track, not re-cited from prior precedent as an earlier draft of this note incorrectly claimed. This track is the first to lock the actual type (ExtractRequest) either finding is about.
reasoning: This track's central methodology risk, checked before drafting: TsconfigMode's Manual(Utf8PathBuf) variant is a data-carrying enum variant on a type with no serde derive at all -- worked out precisely that the absence of Serialize/Deserialize applies uniformly at the enum level regardless of which variant carries data (AC-002), rather than assuming the tuple variant's presence might change the compile-time consequence in some variant-specific way. WorkspaceOptions::new's impl Into<Utf8PathBuf> parameter (AC-004) was checked against the exact verbatim signature rather than assumed to be a plain Utf8PathBuf parameter, since a spec-implementer reading a paraphrased 'takes a path' description could easily under-specify the actual generic signature and its resulting call-site flexibility. AC-006's Default-impl distinction from SPEC-007's established pattern was deliberately worked out rather than pattern-matched by surface similarity ('both involve a type's default behavior') -- SPEC-007's finding is about an impl Default that exists but doesn't wire into serde; this track's finding is that no impl Default exists on TsconfigMode at all, a different and more basic absence that would be wrongly conflated with SPEC-007's finding if stated imprecisely. AC-010 and AC-011 are this track's most valuable findings: rather than treat ExtractRequest as a fresh, unexamined type, checked directly whether either of the two 07-edge-cases findings already cited elsewhere as precedent (by SPEC-006 AC-004, for CodeBlock, a different type) actually name ExtractRequest specifically -- both do, with concrete documented behavioral consequences (a silent empty result; a non-rejected zero value) for ExtractRequest specifically. Corrected during canon-exit-gate's third retry: an earlier draft wrongly claimed CodeBlock's own analogous gap has no documented consequence at all, when SPEC-006 AC-004 (this track's own cited source) documents one -- a defended-against underflow panic, per 01-core-architecture.md:1217-1219 -- that is simply different from ExtractRequest's. The corrected framing states both gaps are documented, with different consequences, rather than drawing a false contrast against a source this spec cites as its own grounding. Kept both criteria's scope carefully limited to what the cited findings actually state (the extract command's own logic that produces these consequences is out of scope, per non_goals), rather than extrapolating into how the consequence is actually implemented, learning directly from SPEC-006 AC-004/AC-011's initial overreach and SPEC-007's AC-014 correction earlier in this session.
